title: Push-button start not working
h1: Why won't my push-button start work?
metaDesc: Push-button start not working or key not detected? Answer a few quick questions to see if it's the fob battery, brake switch, car battery or starter.
synonyms: car wont start with push button
key fob dead how to start car
start button lights up but car wont start
press brake to start but nothing happens
key not recognized car wont start
intro: Push-button start depends on three things: the car detecting your key fob, the brake switch telling it your foot is down, and enough battery power to crank. A message on the dash or what happens when you press the button usually points to which one to check first. Answer the questions below to narrow it down.
safety: If you smell burning plastic or see smoke from the dash or under the hood, stop trying and step away from the car.
Don't press Start over and over with the engine cranking for long periods. Give it a minute between tries.

q_what_happens.q: What happens when you press Start with your foot on the brake?

opts.a: A "Key not detected" message or a key symbol shows on the dash
The dash lights up, but the engine doesn't crank
Nothing at all: no lights, no message, and the doors may not unlock
Rapid clicking, or the dash lights flicker or dim
The engine cranks or starts but then won't keep running

q_remote.q: Does the remote lock and unlock the doors from a normal distance?

opts.a: Only when I'm very close, or not at all

q_spare.q: Have you tried your spare key fob?

opts.a: Yes, and the spare doesn't work either
I don't have a spare / I'm not sure

q_brake.q: Are you pressing the brake firmly, and is the car fully in Park?
q_brake.help: Most push-button cars won't crank unless the brake is pressed (or the clutch, on a manual) and the shifter is all the way in Park or Neutral.

opts.a: Yes, the brake is pressed firmly and it's in Park
Not sure I pressed hard enough, or it may not be fully in Park

q_brake_lights.q: Do the brake lights come on when you press the pedal?
q_brake_lights.help: Ask someone to look, or back up close to a wall or garage door and check for the red glow. Some cars also show a "press brake" message that doesn't go away when you press it.

opts.a: No, the brake lights don't come on

result.title: The key fob battery may be low
result.now: Hold the key fob right against the Start button (or put it in the backup spot your owner's manual shows) and press Start with your foot on the brake. Then replace the fob battery.
if: If it starts with the fob against the button, a new fob battery often fixes it.
If it still says key not detected after a new battery, try the spare fob. If that fails too, the car's key system needs a check.
result.why: The car looks for a weak radio signal from your fob. As the fob battery fades, the car stops detecting it from your pocket. Push-button cars have a backup spot where the fob can still be read with a dead battery.

causes.name: Weak or dead fob battery
causes.clues: The remote's range has been getting shorter, or a low key battery message has appeared.
causes.against: If the remote works normally from a distance, the fob battery is less likely.

causes.name: Signal interference
causes.clues: The fob is near a phone, charger or other electronics, or you're near radio towers or strong transmitters.

causes.name: Damaged key fob
causes.clues: It was dropped or got wet.

you: Hold the fob against the Start button and try again.
Replace the fob battery (often a coin battery). The size is in your owner's manual or inside the fob.
Move the fob away from phones and chargers.

result.title: Your main key fob may be faulty or have lost its programming
result.now: Use the spare for now. Replace the main fob's battery first, and if it still isn't detected, book a dealer or locksmith visit to check or reprogram it.
if: If the main fob was dropped or got wet, it may need replacing. A dealer or locksmith can test it first.
If you only have one working fob left, get a replacement made soon so you aren't stranded.
result.why: If the spare works, the car's key system is probably working and the problem is more likely in the main fob: a dead battery, internal damage, or a chip that's lost its pairing with the car.

causes.name: Dead fob battery
causes.clues: The remote buttons are weak or dead too.
causes.against: If the remote buttons work well from a distance, the battery is less likely.

causes.name: Physical or water damage
causes.clues: The fob was dropped, crushed or went through the wash.

causes.name: Lost programming
causes.clues: It stopped working suddenly, with no damage.

you: Replace the fob battery.
Check the fob for cracks or water damage.

result.title: The car's key detection system or its power may be the problem
result.now: Move phones and chargers away, hold the fob against the Start button and try again. If it still isn't detected, have a dealer or locksmith come to you, or have the car towed to one.
if: If the dash lights are dim or flicker, the car battery may be too weak to run the key system. A jump start may help.
If it works in a different location, something nearby was interfering with the signal.
If the battery is cracked, leaking, swollen or smells like rotten eggs, don't jump start it. Call for roadside help instead.
result.why: When neither fob is detected but both remotes work, the problem is more likely on the car's side: low car battery voltage, interference, or a faulty antenna or key control module.

causes.name: Weak car battery
causes.clues: Dim or flickering lights, or slow cranking recently.

causes.name: Signal interference
causes.clues: It happens in one place, like a parking garage or near transmitters.

causes.name: Faulty key antenna or control module
causes.clues: It fails everywhere, with both fobs and a good battery.

you: Try the fob-against-the-button backup method.
Try a jump start if the lights are dim.
shop: Code scan of the keyless and immobilizer systems

result.title: The car may not be sensing the brake, Park or an unlocked steering wheel
result.now: Press the brake pedal hard and hold it, move the shifter firmly into Park, then press Start. If the steering wheel is locked, gently turn it left and right while you press Start.
if: If it starts in Neutral but not Park, the gear-position switch may be faulty. Book a check.
If it still won't crank with the brake pressed firmly, check whether your brake lights work.
result.why: As a safety feature, push-button cars won't crank unless they sense the brake pedal and Park (or the clutch on a manual). A light press or a shifter not fully in Park is a common reason nothing happens.

causes.name: Brake not pressed firmly enough
causes.clues: It works some days and not others.

causes.name: Shifter not fully in Park
causes.clues: A gear indicator that doesn't show P clearly.

causes.name: Steering lock engaged
causes.clues: The steering wheel won't turn, or a steering lock message appears.

you: Press the brake firmly before pressing Start.
Try starting in Neutral.
Wiggle the steering wheel while pressing Start.

result.title: A faulty brake light switch may be blocking the start
result.now: Don't drive the car until the brake lights work: drivers behind you get no warning when you brake. Have the brake light circuit checked within the next few days.
if: If only one brake light is out, that's a bulb, not the switch. Look at whether all of them stay dark.
If you need to move the car before it's fixed, a mobile mechanic can often test and repair the brake light circuit where the car sits.
If the brake pedal feels soft or sinks, or the red brake warning light is on, don't drive it until the brakes have been checked.
result.why: The car uses the brake light switch to know your foot is on the pedal. If none of the brake lights come on, the switch is a common cause, though a fuse or wiring fault can do the same. A shop will usually check the fuse and wiring before replacing the switch. Either way the car won't let you start it, and drivers behind you get no warning when you brake.

causes.name: Failed brake light switch
causes.clues: No brake lights at all, and a press-brake message that won't clear.

causes.name: Blown brake light fuse
causes.clues: Brake lights and other items on the same fuse stopped working together.

causes.name: Loose switch or wiring at the pedal
causes.clues: It works sometimes depending on how hard you press.

you: Have someone check whether any brake lights come on.
Check the brake light fuse listed in your owner's manual.
shop: Brake light circuit and fuse check

result.title: The starter, a weak battery or the Park switch may be the problem
result.now: Try starting in Neutral with the brake pressed. If that doesn't work, try a jump start. If it still won't crank, have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If it starts in Neutral but not Park, that points toward the gear-position switch or its adjustment.
If it starts with a jump, have the battery and charging system tested soon.
If the battery is cracked, leaking, swollen or smells like rotten eggs, don't jump start it. Call for roadside help instead.
If you smell burning or see smoke after trying to start it, stop trying and step away from the car.
result.why: With the key detected and the brake working, the car is ready to crank, but the starter isn't turning the engine. That points to a battery too weak to crank, a gear-position switch not reporting Park, or a failing starter.

causes.name: Weak battery
causes.clues: Dim lights, a slow crank recently, or a battery more than 4 years old.
causes.against: If the lights stay bright while pressing Start, the battery is less likely.

causes.name: Gear-position (Park/Neutral) switch
causes.clues: It starts in Neutral but not Park.

causes.name: Failing starter
causes.clues: A single click, or starting has been hit-or-miss lately.

you: Try starting in Neutral.
Try a jump start or booster pack.

result.title: The car's main battery is probably dead
result.now: Use the metal key hidden inside your fob to open the driver's door, then jump start the car or use a battery booster.
if: If the battery is cracked, leaking, swollen or smells like rotten eggs, don't jump start it. Call for roadside help instead.
If a jump works, drive at least 30 minutes or have the battery and charging system tested soon.
If nothing happens even with a good jump, a main fuse or cable may have failed. It will need a tow or a mobile mechanic.
On a hybrid or electric car, check your owner's manual for where to connect jumper cables before you start.
If the battery light comes on while driving after a jump, the charging system may not be working. Have it checked before relying on the car.
result.why: With no lights and no response, the car has no power to run the key system or the starter. The usual reason is a drained 12-volt battery, which many push-button cars have even if they're hybrid or electric.

causes.name: Drained or dead 12-volt battery
causes.clues: Lights left on, the car sat for weeks, cold weather, or an older battery.

causes.name: Loose or corroded battery cable
causes.clues: Crusty buildup on the terminals, or a loose clamp.

causes.name: Blown main fuse
causes.clues: A jump start changes nothing at all.
causes.against: Much less common than a battery problem.

you: Check the battery terminals for corrosion or loose clamps.
Try a jump start or booster pack.
shop: Parasitic draw test if the battery keeps dying

result.title: The battery may be too weak to crank the engine
result.now: Check that the battery clamps are tight and clean, then try a jump start or a battery booster.
if: If the battery is cracked, leaking, swollen or smells like rotten eggs, don't jump start it. Call for roadside help instead.
If it starts with a jump, have the battery and alternator tested soon.
If it still only clicks with a good jump, the cables or starter are the more likely problem.
result.why: Rapid clicking or flickering lights mean there's enough power to run the dash, but not enough to spin the starter. A weak battery can also cause key-not-detected messages because the key system needs steady voltage.

causes.name: Weak or discharged battery
causes.clues: Dim lights, cold weather, or a battery more than 4 years old.

causes.name: Corroded or loose battery terminal
causes.clues: Visible buildup, or the clicking changes when you wiggle a cable.

causes.name: Alternator not charging
causes.clues: The battery light came on recently while driving.

you: Check the battery terminals.
Try a jump start or a booster pack.
shop: Voltage-drop test on the battery cables

result.title: The key system or fuel delivery may be stopping the engine
result.now: Look for a flashing key or security light, and try the spare fob. If it still won't keep running, have the codes read or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If the spare fob works, replace the main fob's battery or have it checked.
If you smell raw fuel, stop trying to start it and keep flames away.
result.why: If the engine cranks or fires and then dies, the button and starter are working. The anti-theft system cutting fuel because it doesn't recognize the key is common, followed by fuel or idle problems.

causes.name: Immobilizer not recognizing the key
causes.clues: A flashing key or security light, or it works with one fob but not the other.

causes.name: Fuel delivery problem
causes.clues: No hum from the rear when the car is switched on, or low fuel.

causes.name: Idle control or sensor problem
causes.clues: A check engine light, or a rough idle before it dies.

you: Try the spare fob.
Watch for a security light.
